attributes.residual: REVERTED, and the reversion is the finding. On setWorldParms this identical edit held the instruction count EXACTLY equal (843/843) while improving the multiset 40t -> 32t and fuzzy 95.4626 -> 95.5101, so it was a free structural win. On MBNewPsysDescrip the same edit cost FOUR instructions (793 -> 797), drove real 496 -> 610, improved the multiset further (40t -> 30t), and moved fresh-report fuzzy only 95.6747 -> 95.7629. It was banked with probe.py --rebase-best, then deliberately reverted: the defake gate goes red on real, project-level metrics are unchanged either way (All 98.29% fuzzy / 64.42% matched with and without it), and this function's realistic route to EXACT is the WebFrank recolor path - 184 regnorm RENAMING rows against only 15 genuine structural rows - for which count parity is a hard precondition. Trading count parity for 0.088 fuzzy points forecloses the more valuable option. THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON: the ternary-diamond lever's COUNT COST is a per-function register-pressure property, not a property of the source pattern. Two functions in one TU with a row-for-row identical residual and a character-for-character identical edit priced it differently - free on one, four instructions on the other - so the IH law's cost note ('the rewrite ADDS one instruction per site') must be re-measured per function and cannot be predicted from a matching residual signature. Reopen this site only with a lever for the two surplus per-group `fmr` copies in hand, so the count can be paid for rather than merely spent.
